P11-001.challenge_claim: The row's only rear-edge warrant carries an explicit byte-tier label with nothing collated behind it, and the postpositive contrast blends two distinct censuses without a digit, a named object or a quoted form.
P11-001.grounds: Verified in the row's favour first, and it is a substantial list: the frame parent and the frame seam at MT 39:8 | MT 40:1 are handled correctly and the row does not straddle it; the petuchah at MT 39:8 and the setumah at MT 40:2 are correctly typed and never conflated; chs 39-40 are identity numbering so no dual or numeric qualifier is owed; no ketiv/qere note falls in the span; both WEB runs are verbatim; and the attribution of the plural comforters is honestly held open rather than assigned - which is right, since the herald-voice attribution across MT 40:1-11 is a question a chunking row never decides. Nothing below touches it. (1) UPHELD, and it is the cleanest defect of the five rows. The rejected-alternative sentence cites oshb:Isa.40.3 with an explicit 'tier: byte' label and quotes no Hebrew at all - a tier asserted with nothing collated behind it, which is the tier-disclosure standard breached at its plainest. The form the argument needs was available and is two tokens long: MT 40:3 opens ק֣וֹל קוֹרֵ֔א (oshb:Isa.40.3, byte), the sole site of that herald onset in the book (sweep: 1 verse, byte and finals-normalized skeleton alike). (2) UPHELD. 'the tetragrammaton signature used in most of the book's postpositive formulas' carries no digit, names no swept object, and blends two censuses that must stay apart: the postpositive oracle signature (23 verses book-wide, whose only narrative-zone site is MT 37:34's נְאֻם יְהוָֽה, byte tier) and the amar-plus-tetragrammaton adjacency (52 verses). The row's own inquit, יֹאמַ֖ר אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.40.1, byte), is the Elohim variant and is excluded from the adjacency census outright - which is the fact the contrast actually needs and the one it never states. No contrast form is quoted, so a comparison the row makes its onset argument out of stands on English alone, and 'most' is a quantifier with no digit behind it. (3) UPHELD. The PLURAL number of the imperatives is the hinge of the unnamed-comforters reading and is never named: נַחֲמ֥וּ נַחֲמ֖וּ at MT 40:1 and דַּבְּר֞וּ with וְקִרְא֣וּ at MT 40:2 (byte tier) are spliced but described only as 'a doubled imperative command' and as 'addressed to unnamed comforters'. With no morphology layer staged, the plural is nonetheless carried in the letter bytes and in both witnesses' renderings, so it is a byte-checkable claim the row leaves unstated while resting an argument on it. NEW FINDING (raised by neither primary): device_notes grounds its unit_type handling in a governance allowance - 'per the operative-category allowance for the closed unit_type vocabulary'. That is the same register class the challenge flags in the sibling hymn row of this cluster, and it is unflagged here, so it is also an internal asymmetry across the pair: a governance rule may govern the row, but it may not stand in row prose as the row's stated warrant.
P11-001.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: splice the herald onset at oshb:Isa.40.3 and let the existing tier label rest on collated bytes; add its digit (sweep: 1 verse book-wide). The sentence must name the FORM only - the rival is a fresh voice-onset - and must NOT assign the speaker, since the herald-voice attribution stays open. One sentence, plus at most a second carrying the rival disclosure. boundary_rationale: re-cut the postpositive contrast so it names ONE object and carries a digit. State that the row's inquit is the Elohim variant, excluded from the amar-plus-tetragrammaton adjacency census (52 verses), and keep the postpositive oracle-signature census (23 verses) separate; quote the contrast form if the contrast is retained. Delete the undigited 'most'. boundary_rationale or device_notes: name the plural number of the imperatives at oshb:Isa.40.1 and oshb:Isa.40.2 as a byte-checkable form claim, since the plural addressee is what the unnamed-comforters reading rests on - naming the FORM only, never the referent, which stays held open. device_notes (NEW FINDING cure): replace the governance-allowance appeal with the substantive ground for the unit_type call, argued from the bytes of the onset. The vocabulary rule remains binding; it may not be the row's stated warrant. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: the tier and count-object checks that killed the original - every 'tier: byte' label in the row must have a collated pointed run behind it; the postpositive comparison must name a single swept object with a digit and must not blend the 23-verse signature census with the 52-verse adjacency census; and no field may cite a governance allowance as the row's warrant.

P11-002.challenge_claim: The opening cut is argued as a clean speaker break while two byte-grounded lexical hooks run straight across that seam undisclosed.
P11-002.grounds: Re-derived from bytes, both hooks are real and both are decision-relevant. Object one, the second-person-plural divine title: אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.40.1) re-collates against oshb:Isa.40.9 at BYTE tier and reciprocally, and the object is distinctive rather than a generic divine name -- that word-bound form stands in only 4 verses book-wide, 2 of them the pair here (sweep: 4 verses, the 2mp-suffixed Elohim form, skeleton tier; chs 40-41 = oshb:Isa.40.1 and oshb:Isa.40.9). Its first-person-plural counterpart runs between them: לֵאלֹהֵֽינוּ closes this row's own opening verse (oshb:Isa.40.3, byte tier against its own verse) and אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ (oshb:Isa.40.8, byte tier against its own verse) re-collates against oshb:Isa.40.3 at skeleton tier. Object two, the calling root, named by attested form because the plene participle is not a contiguous match for the three-letter skeleton and the skeleton sweep does not return oshb:Isa.40.3 at all (sweep: 7 verses, contiguous qr' skeleton, chs 40-41 -- oshb:Isa.40.2, 40.6, 40.26, 41.2, 41.4, 41.9, 41.25): וְקִרְא֣וּ (oshb:Isa.40.2) then קוֹרֵ֔א (oshb:Isa.40.3) then קְרָ֔א and אֶקְרָ֑א (oshb:Isa.40.6), each byte tier against its own verse. Both objects straddle both of this row's seams, and the rejected alternative rests precisely on discontinuity at web:Isa.40.2|web:Isa.40.3 while engaging neither. Under the cross-seam cohesion rule a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity unless disclosed, so the defect is real. Credit stands where OL gave it: the two single-witness SAMEKH marks at oshb:Isa.40.2 and oshb:Isa.40.5 (tier-3) verify under the claimed type, both splices are byte tier, and leaving the crier unnamed is byte-sound. Severity low is correct -- this is a disclosure gap, not an overturned cut.
P11-002.remedy: device_notes: add one cross-seam disclosure sentence naming both straddling objects with pointed splices and collate-true tiers -- the 2mp title אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.40.1) against oshb:Isa.40.9 at byte tier, its 1cp counterpart לֵאלֹהֵֽינוּ (oshb:Isa.40.3) / אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ (oshb:Isa.40.8) at skeleton tier, and the calling-root chain וְקִרְא֣וּ (oshb:Isa.40.2), קוֹרֵ֔א (oshb:Isa.40.3), קְרָ֔א and אֶקְרָ֑א (oshb:Isa.40.6), byte tier each against its own verse -- and state why the speaker-onset ground survives them. observed_substrate_signals: add the dotted keys for the signal classes newly consulted (divine_title.* and refrain.*), as dependent fields of the added disclosure. No respan; the cut is not challenged. TEST the cure must pass: re-collation of every added run must return exactly the tier written (the pair at oshb:Isa.40.1/oshb:Isa.40.9 must return byte and the 1cp pair must return skeleton, not byte), and a cross-seam re-check of web:Isa.40.2|web:Isa.40.3 must return no byte-true device left undisclosed -- the check that killed the original is that the seam argument stood on speaker discontinuity alone while a byte-identical title pair bracketed the row.

P11-003.challenge_claim: The row's principal cohesion evidence, the repeated withering-grass clause, is stated through the English with no Hebrew form and no tier, and it is not byte-recurrent.
P11-003.grounds: Verified in both directions: יָבֵ֤שׁ חָצִיר֙ נָ֣בֵֽל צִ֔יץ (oshb:Isa.40.7) against oshb:Isa.40.8 returns accent_stripped, and יָבֵ֥שׁ חָצִ֖יר נָ֣בֵֽל צִ֑יץ (oshb:Isa.40.8) against oshb:Isa.40.7 returns accent_stripped -- letters and vowels agree, the accents differ, so the clause is NOT byte-recurrent. The row carries this, its own load-bearing intra-unit cohesion ground, entirely in English ('the clause translated ...'), with no splice and no tier on a recurrence claim; the tier-disclosure standard requires every recurrence claim to be tier-labelled at write time, so the claim is defective as written and simultaneously understates evidence that is genuinely there at accent_stripped tier. The quote/gloss parity slip verifies too: the row's opening splice runs the whole of oshb:Isa.40.6 through כְּצִ֥יץ הַשָּׂדֶֽה while its paired curly-quoted English stops at the second question, and the WEB verse continues past that point (web:Isa.40.6). Cross-seam, the row splices אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ at its own closing verse without disclosing that this is the middle member of the byte-tier title pair אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.40.1) / oshb:Isa.40.9 that brackets the row's close. Mark handling is correct and verifies under the claimed type: SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.40.5 before the span and SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.40.8 at its close (tier-3, single-witness). Severity medium is right: the defect sits on the row's principal cohesion driver, not on a decorative aside.
P11-003.remedy: device_notes: replace the English-only refrain sentence with a spliced, tier-labelled one -- יָבֵ֤שׁ חָצִיר֙ נָ֣בֵֽל צִ֔יץ (oshb:Isa.40.7) re-collates against oshb:Isa.40.8 at accent_stripped tier and reciprocally, agreeing in letters and vowels and differing in the accents, expressly NOT byte. boundary_rationale: re-cut the gloss at the opening verse so the curly-quoted WEB run and the pointed splice cover the same extent -- either carry the English through the flower-of-the-field clause (web:Isa.40.6) or trim the splice to אֶקְרָ֑א; a quote/gloss parity repair re-cuts the gloss, it does not re-cut the splice alone. device_notes: add the cross-seam disclosure of the byte-tier title pair אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.40.1) / oshb:Isa.40.9 straddling this row's close. TEST the cure must pass: re-collation of the refrain pair must return accent_stripped, so any 'byte', 'verbatim' or 'byte-identical' wording fails -- that is the check that killed the original -- and a quote/gloss extent re-check at the opening verse must show the English and the pointed run ending at the same clause.

P11-004.challenge_claim: The rejected alternative asserts a form-class fact the bytes contradict: neither an imperative nor a feminine-singular addressee carries forward into web:Isa.40.10-Isa.40.11.
P11-004.grounds: The refuted sentence is the row's own strongest_rejected_alternative, which states that 'the imperative and addressee both carry forward unchanged from web:Isa.40.9'. Re-derived from the pointed bytes, the two following verses carry no imperative and no second-person form of any gender: יָב֔וֹא (oshb:Isa.40.10) under a presentative, then יִרְעֶ֔ה, יְקַבֵּ֣ץ, יִשָּׂ֑א and יְנַהֵֽל (oshb:Isa.40.11), each byte tier against its own verse, all third-masculine-singular yiqtol. The one feminine form in the pair, the participle מֹ֣שְׁלָה (oshb:Isa.40.10), agrees with the feminine arm-noun standing beside it in the same clause, and both witnesses render it of the arm and not of an addressee (web:Isa.40.10). Form-class labels are byte-checkable claims under the same discipline as digits, so this is a defect, not a reading preference. The herald address itself is byte-sound as the row has it (אַל תִּירָ֔אִי and the 2fs suffixes, oshb:Isa.40.9, byte tier). Two further arms verify: neither following verse is spliced at all, so the continuity ground is carried in English alone, and the byte-tier title pair אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.40.1) against oshb:Isa.40.9 straddles this row's opening seam undisclosed. Marks at oshb:Isa.40.8 and oshb:Isa.40.11 verify under the claimed type (SAMEKH, tier-3, single-witness). The cut is NOT overturned -- the row's other ground survives and is byte-supported by the presentative chain -- but its stated warrant is false, so medium stands.
P11-004.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: delete the clause asserting that the imperative and the addressee carry forward unchanged, and replace it with the byte-true continuity warrant -- the presentative particle carries the herald's commanded announcement across the verses, הִנֵּ֖ה (oshb:Isa.40.9) re-collating against oshb:Isa.40.10 at accent_stripped tier where it stands twice, הִנֵּ֨ה and הִנֵּ֤ה (oshb:Isa.40.10, byte tier against its own verse) -- keeping the one-sentence limit plus the optional mandated-rival sentence. device_notes: splice at least one form from each of oshb:Isa.40.10 and oshb:Isa.40.11 with its tier, and record that מֹ֣שְׁלָה is feminine by agreement with the arm-noun beside it rather than by any addressee, per both witnesses' renderings (web:Isa.40.10). device_notes: disclose the byte-tier title pair אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.40.1) / oshb:Isa.40.9 across the opening seam. TEST the replacement warrant must pass: it must survive the exact check that killed the original -- every form-class label in it re-checked against the pointed bytes and both witnesses' renderings, with the revised sentence containing no claim of a carried-forward imperative or of any second-person addressee in web:Isa.40.10-Isa.40.11, and every added run re-collating to the tier written.

P11-005.challenge_claim: The interrogative is used as an intra-unit cohesion argument while the same word-bound interrogative continues across this row's closing seam at three further sites (sweep: 3 verses), undisclosed.
P11-005.grounds: Object and tier both verify. The row argues that 'the interrogative form recurs at web:Isa.40.13-Isa.40.14 as an internal chain rather than a fresh onset', i.e. it uses the interrogative as an intra-unit cohesion signal. Re-derived word-bound -- the two-letter token matched whole-token against the consonantal skeletons and never as a substring -- the same token stands in 9 verses across chs 40-41 (sweep: 9 verses: oshb:Isa.40.12, 40.13, 40.14, 40.18, 40.25, 40.26, 41.2, 41.4, 41.26). Three of those sit immediately past this row's close, and two of them are structural in the next row: וְאֶל מִ֖י opens oshb:Isa.40.18, וְאֶל מִ֥י closes oshb:Isa.40.25, and וּרְאוּ֙ מִי stands mid-verse at oshb:Isa.40.26 (byte tier each against its own verse), against מִֽי at this row's own onset (oshb:Isa.40.12, byte tier). A signal that runs on immediately past the seam cannot by itself distinguish inside from outside, and the row discloses none of it while resting the same seam on the absence of a form or addressee shift. The two secondary arms verify as well: the closing verse is argued in English only, with no pointed splice for oshb:Isa.40.17, and an MT-keyed single-witness mark annotation is hung on a WEB-prefixed coordinate at web:Isa.40.16 while the correct oshb:Isa.40.16 entry also stands. Credit where OL gave it, and I re-derived it independently: the interior mark is held as presence only, and the row's statement that the next mark does not recur until oshb:Isa.40.24 is TRUE against the single-witness layer, which carries nothing at oshb:Isa.40.17 through oshb:Isa.40.23. Severity low is correct.
P11-005.remedy: device_notes: disclose that the word-bound interrogative continues past this row's close at oshb:Isa.40.18, oshb:Isa.40.25 and oshb:Isa.40.26 (sweep: 9 verses, word-bound interrogative token, chs 40-41), and name the tier-1 signal that actually distinguishes the units, since the interrogative alone does not. boundary_rationale: supply a pointed splice with its tier for the closing verse oshb:Isa.40.17, so the close is argued in the original language and not in English alone. boundary_evidence_refs: delete the entry 'web:Isa.40.16 (SAMEKH, single-witness)' -- that layer is MT-keyed and the correctly keyed oshb:Isa.40.16 entry already stands, so the WEB-prefixed one is both mis-witnessed and a duplicate. TEST the cure must pass: a span-relevant mark-disclosure symmetry sweep must show every parashah annotation carried on an oshb: key only and under its claimed type; the interrogative citation must name its swept object and unit and carry a digit; and the verified-true statement that no mark falls at oshb:Isa.40.17-oshb:Isa.40.23 must survive the edit unchanged.

P11-006.challenge_claim: The envelope driver is a real and exclusive object, but it is tier-labeled byte when the two verses do not recur at any tier.
P11-006.grounds: The defect is real but the framing overstates it in one direction and understates the row's hedge in the other. Verified: the full runs וְאֶל מִ֖י תְּדַמְּי֣וּן (oshb:Isa.40.18) against oshb:Isa.40.25 and וְאֶל מִ֥י תְדַמְּי֖וּנִי (oshb:Isa.40.25) against oshb:Isa.40.18 both return tier NONE, the verbs differing in the dagesh and in the first-person suffix -- so a 'tier: byte' label written over that pair is wrong. But 'do not recur at any tier' is itself byte-false: the shared two-word interrogative prefix וְאֶל מִ֖י (oshb:Isa.40.18) re-collates against oshb:Isa.40.25 at accent_stripped tier. The corrected finding: the envelope is real, its recurrent portion is the interrogative prefix at accent_stripped tier and the verb pair is NOT recurrent at any tier, and the row's single joint 'tier: byte' parenthesis conflates the two while its own trailing words ('matching construction rather than an identical full clause') expressly deny identity -- an ambiguous and mislocated tier label rather than a false byte-identity assertion, which is why severity is low and not medium. OL's exclusivity digit verifies (sweep: 2 verses, contiguous liken-root skeleton, chs 40-41: oshb:Isa.40.18 and oshb:Isa.40.25; 3 verses book-wide). The remaining arms verify: the cross-seam echo at web:Isa.40.21|web:Isa.40.28 is carried with no splice and no tier (and does not recur in the Hebrew at any tier -- see this cluster's high-severity row); the closing splice carries the frame יֹאמַ֖ר קָדֽוֹשׁ (oshb:Isa.40.25, byte tier) while observed_substrate_signals names no speech-formula or divine-title key; and an MT-keyed mark is again hung on a WEB coordinate at web:Isa.40.24 beside the correct oshb: entry. The row is right not to count that bare epithet as a title site: the objects separate in the bytes (sweep: 4 verses, contiguous qadosh skeleton, chs 40-41 -- the bare epithet at oshb:Isa.40.25 against the full title at oshb:Isa.41.14, oshb:Isa.41.16 and oshb:Isa.41.20).
P11-006.remedy: boundary_rationale: split the one joint tier label into two collate-true labels -- the shared interrogative prefix וְאֶל מִ֖י (oshb:Isa.40.18) against oshb:Isa.40.25 at accent_stripped tier, and the full runs וְאֶל מִ֖י תְּדַמְּי֣וּן / וְאֶל מִ֥י תְדַמְּי֖וּנִי at tier NONE in both directions -- and drop 'tier: byte' from the envelope parenthesis entirely. device_notes: tier-label the cross-seam echo at web:Isa.40.21|web:Isa.40.28 or drop the recurrence framing, since it is NONE at every tier and the resemblance is a rendering fact. observed_substrate_signals: add the speech_formula.* / divine_title.* key for the frame יֹאמַ֖ר קָדֽוֹשׁ the closing splice already carries. boundary_evidence_refs: delete 'web:Isa.40.24 (SAMEKH, single-witness)', the MT-keyed layer wrongly witnessed, the correct oshb:Isa.40.24 entry standing. TEST the cure must pass: every recurrence label must equal the tier returned for the exact run quoted, so 'byte' may appear only where re-collation returns byte -- the check that killed the original -- and the mark-disclosure symmetry sweep must find no parashah annotation on a WEB key.

P11-007.challenge_claim: OL: a parashah division falls after this span's own opening verse at exactly the cut the row names and rejects and is not disclosed, and a cross-seam recurrence is tier-labeled byte although it does not recur in the Hebrew at any tier. LF: the row never discloses that its own opening verse carries a parashah mark, though it types every other cited mark, and the silent gap sits exactly where its rejected alternative needed it most.
P11-007.grounds: The two primaries hit the SAME defect by independent routes, and it is confirmed: the single-witness mark layer carries a SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.40.26 (tier-3), a division after this span's own opening verse, which is exactly the web:Isa.40.26|web:Isa.40.27 cut the row's strongest_rejected_alternative names and dismisses on content grounds alone. The row cites oshb:Isa.40.26 bare in boundary_evidence_refs while typing oshb:Isa.40.31 as PE, so span-relevant mark symmetry is broken at the one verse in the span where the layer is decision-relevant, and it is broken in the direction that corroborates the rival being refused. Absence would never be counterevidence, but a mark present inside the span is owed. OL's three further defects are distinct and all verify. (2) The tier label is false: הֲל֤וֹא תֵֽדְעוּ֙ (oshb:Isa.40.21) against oshb:Isa.40.28 and הֲל֨וֹא יָדַ֜עְתָּ אִם לֹ֣א שָׁמַ֗עְתָּ (oshb:Isa.40.28) against oshb:Isa.40.21 both return tier NONE -- second-masculine-plural imperfect against second-masculine-singular perfect, and the later verse's second question is introduced by a conditional-negative pair rather than by the interrogative particle standing four times in the earlier one. The identity is a rendering fact only: both WEB verses open “Haven’t you known? Haven’t you heard?” (web:Isa.40.21, web:Isa.40.28), and the row's device_notes writes 'tier: byte' over that pair with no Hebrew quoted anywhere. (3) The closing seam is straddled undisclosed: יַחֲלִ֣יפוּ כֹ֔חַ (oshb:Isa.40.31) re-collates against oshb:Isa.41.1 at accent_stripped tier and reciprocally, a catchword at the oracle join arguing continuity against the cut. (4) A paseq seg sits at oshb:Isa.40.28 (count-only, single-witness), a verse the row cites in evidence, undisclosed. Credit stands: both pointed splices are byte tier and the imperative onset שְׂאוּ מָר֨וֹם עֵינֵיכֶ֤ם (oshb:Isa.40.26, byte tier) is byte-sound. Four real defects, one of them at the decision point of the row's own rejected rival and one a false byte label on a recurrence with no Hebrew behind it: high is correct.
P11-007.remedy: boundary_evidence_refs: type the mark at the span's own opening verse as 'oshb:Isa.40.26 (SAMEKH, single-witness)'. strongest_rejected_alternative: weigh that mark explicitly where the web:Isa.40.26|web:Isa.40.27 cut is refused -- name it as tier-3 single-witness corroboration standing FOR the rival, and refuse the rival on the tier-1 ground (the imperative onset supplying the evidence the complaint is answered by), never by silence; if the writer concludes the mark plus the onset shift now favour the cut, that is a boundary PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption and is not author work. device_notes: strike 'tier: byte' from the rebuke recurrence and state the collate truth -- הֲל֤וֹא תֵֽדְעוּ֙ (oshb:Isa.40.21) against oshb:Isa.40.28 and הֲל֨וֹא יָדַ֜עְתָּ אִם לֹ֣א שָׁמַ֗עְתָּ (oshb:Isa.40.28) against oshb:Isa.40.21 both at tier NONE, the shared question pair being a rendering fact at web:Isa.40.21 and web:Isa.40.28. device_notes: disclose the closing-seam catchword יַחֲלִ֣יפוּ כֹ֔חַ (oshb:Isa.40.31) against oshb:Isa.41.1 at accent_stripped tier. device_notes or boundary_evidence_refs: disclose the paseq at oshb:Isa.40.28 as count-only and single-witness, asserting no intra-verse position. TEST the cure must pass: a span-relevant mark-disclosure symmetry sweep across oshb:Isa.40.26-oshb:Isa.40.31 must return no remainder, with each mark under its claimed type and PE never conflated with SAMEKH, and the paseq tallied; and re-collation of every recurrence run must return exactly the tier written -- the check that killed the original is that 'tier: byte' on the rebuke pair fails at every tier, so any surviving byte or verbatim wording there re-fails.

P11-008.challenge_claim: OL: a single-witness Prophets parashah mark is placed in the operative position of the rejected alternative, and the span's opening seam is straddled by an undisclosed catchword. LF: the row folds a third-person craftsmen vignette into a second-person judicial summons and first-person divine self-declaration without weighing the speech-register shift between them as a candidate seam, testing only a weaker rejected alternative instead.
P11-008.grounds: The two items are PARTLY the same defect and partly distinct, and one distinct arm is refuted. Same defect, reached by two routes and upheld: the row's strongest_rejected_alternative refuses the earlier close 'because the parashah SAMEKH mark closes the whole complex specifically at oshb:Isa.41.7', putting a tier-3 single-witness Prophets mark in the driving position with the content ground trailing behind an 'and'; LF states the same thing as the mark not settling whether a tier-1 frame shift sits inside that paragraph. In the Prophets that layer is corroboration only, never a boundary driver, so the sentence is defective as ordered. REFUTED, on the row's own bytes and its own text: LF's claim that the sharper register seam was 'never engag[ed]' does not hold.
